annotation.title_clean: Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 on the safety of toys and repealing Directive 2009/48/EC
annotation.title_en: Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 on the safety of toys and repealing Directive 2009/48/EC
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: EU Regulation replacing the Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC. It sets essential safety requirements for toys for children under 14, tightens chemical rules (PFAS, bisphenols, CMR substances), and introduces a digital product passport. It also covers conformity assessment and online marketplace duties. AI-enabled and connected toys are routed to the AI Act and Cyber Resilience Act.
key_provisions_or_claims: General and particular safety requirements for toys, including foreseeable use and children's behaviour
Generic prohibitions on CMR substances, endocrine disruptors, PFAS and 34 bisphenols
Mandatory digital product passport replacing the EU declaration of conformity, kept 10 years
Connected and AI toys must comply with the AI Act and Regulation 2024/2847; digitally connected toys' safety assessment must consider mental health risks
Obligations for manufacturers, importers, distributors, fulfilment providers and online marketplaces; notified body rules
